This vignette shows how to compare more than two states, whole regions, and whole time courses.
For data checks, see `vignette("data_quality")`.

## The significance rule

All functions use the same rule (Hageman & Weis, Anal. Chem. 2019):
a peptide differs between two states when its Welch t-test p-value is below `pvalue` **and** the difference is larger than the critical interval (CI).

-   `p_adjust = "BH"` corrects the p-values for multiple testing.
-   `percent = "per_residue"` divides uptake by the number of exchangeable residues, so peptide length does not affect the result.

## Which function for which question

| Function | Question |
|---|---|
| `compare_states_tp()` | Does this peptide differ between states? (3+ states) |
| `compare_regions()` | Does this region differ between states? |
| `compare_states_unmatched()` | Does this region differ, when the states have different peptides? |
| `compare_timecourse()` | Does this peptide differ over the whole time course? |
| `residue_regions()` | Which stretches of residues changed? |

For two states at one time point, `plot_fissure_vent()` and `diff_peptides_prep()` are the main tools.

## `compare_states_tp()`: peptides, three or more states

```{r}
library(HDXBoxeR)
file_nm <- system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
file_3state <- system.file("extdata", "three_states.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
```

`three_states.csv` has a wild-type protein and two point mutants (D109H, R120G), with 3-4 replicates (Woods et al. 2025, PNAS).

```{r}
res <- compare_states_tp(file_3state, times = "1800.00s")
head(res)
```

Each row is one peptide and one pair of states.
`p_omnibus` is a Welch ANOVA across all states.
It is given for information; `is_sig` uses the rule above for each pair.

Compare every state to one reference only:

```{r}
res_ref <- compare_states_tp(file_3state, times = "1800.00s", reference = "WT_pH7.5")
unique(res_ref[, c("state1", "state2")])
```

Peptides that cover a mutation have a different sequence in the mutant.
`by = "position"` matches peptides by position, so these peptides are compared too:

```{r}
res_pos <- compare_states_tp(file_3state, times = "1800.00s", reference = "WT_pH7.5", by = "position")
c(by_sequence = nrow(res_ref), by_position = nrow(res_pos))
```

Split by regions:

```{r}
res_regions <- compare_states_tp(file_3state, times = "1800.00s", reference = "WT_pH7.5",
                                 regions = list(nterm = c(1, 90), cterm = c(91, 175)))
table(res_regions$region)
```

```{r, fig.height = 6}
plot_compare_states_tp(res_regions, plot_type = "jitter")
```

Every peptide is shown; significant ones are colored.
`plot_type = "box"` or `"violin"` adds a summary shape.

## `compare_regions()`: a whole region

`compare_regions()` tests whether the states differ in a region.
Each peptide is its own control: the model is `uptake ~ peptide + state` on the peptide averages.
For two states this is a paired t-test of the peptide differences.
The peptides must be found in every state.

```{r}
reg <- compare_regions(file_nm, times = "1800.00s",
                       regions = list(nterm = c(1, 100), cterm = c(101, 225)))
reg$summary
reg$pairs
```

-   `p_state`: do the states differ in this region?
-   `p_state_x_peptide`: does the difference change from peptide to peptide? If yes, the effect is local - look at the single peptides.
-   `estimate`: the average difference per peptide (state2 - state1).

Here cterm differs clearly (p = 0.0006).
nterm is borderline (p = 0.08): some of its peptides change and some do not.

All time points in one model, with a test for state x time:

```{r}
compare_regions(file_nm, regions = list(nterm = c(1, 100), cterm = c(101, 225)),
                time_model = TRUE)$summary
```

## `compare_states_unmatched()`: different peptides in the states

Use this function when the states do not share the same peptides.
All peptides in a region are pooled per state, and the states are compared.
`regions` is required.

```{r}
res_unmatched <- compare_states_unmatched(file_nm, times = "1800.00s",
                                          regions = list(nterm = c(1, 100), cterm = c(101, 225)))
res_unmatched$summary
res_unmatched$coverage
```

Read the first columns first: `frac_peptides_significant` is the fraction of the shared peptides that differ by the rule above.
The pooled test after it is only approximate.

Here the pooled test is not significant (p = 0.29 and 0.58), but 5/9 nterm peptides and 6/19 cterm peptides differ.
A non-significant pooled result does **not** mean nothing changed.

`frac_shared_all_states` in `coverage` is the fraction of peptides found in every state.
If it is low, a difference can come from different peptides rather than different exchange.

```{r, fig.height = 6}
plot_coverage_diagnostics(res_unmatched)
```

```{r, fig.height = 5}
plot_compare_states_unmatched(res_unmatched, plot_type = "jitter",
                              state_labels = c(Unbound = "Unbound", bound = "Bound"))
```

More than two states work the same way, and the mutant peptides are included:

```{r, fig.height = 6}
res3_unmatched <- compare_states_unmatched(file_3state, times = "1800.00s",
                                           regions = list(nterm = c(1, 90), cterm = c(91, 175)))
plot_compare_states_unmatched(res3_unmatched, plot_type = "jitter")
```

Options:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
## values: uptake in Da (default), percent, or uptake per exchangeable residue
compare_states_unmatched(file_nm, times = "1800.00s", regions = list(nterm = c(1, 100)), value = "frac_deut")
## methods: "peptide" (default), "resample" (permutation p-values and bootstrap CI),
## "classic" (every replicate pooled; only to reproduce old analyses)
compare_states_unmatched(file_nm, times = "1800.00s", regions = list(nterm = c(1, 100)),
                         method = "resample", seed = 1)
```

## `compare_timecourse()`: the whole time course

`compare_timecourse()` judges each peptide on all time points together.
It gives the summed difference over time with its own CI, and the number of time points where the peptide is significant.

```{r}
tc <- compare_timecourse(file_nm, "Unbound", "bound")
head(tc[order(tc$p_value), c("Start", "End", "summed_delta", "p_value", "ci_sum",
                             "sig_summed", "n_timepoints_sig")])
```

Robot plots can show only peptides significant at two or more time points: `robot_plot_All(..., min_timepoints = 2)`.

## `residue_regions()`: stretches of residues

`residue_regions()` finds stretches of residues that changed in the same direction.
A residue is included when at least `min_peptides` (default 2) significant peptides cover it.
The effect is given per exchangeable residue.

```{r}
a_da <- output_tp(file_nm)
rr <- residue_regions(a_da, state1 = "Unbound", state2 = "bound", times = "1800.00s")
rr
```

Check the regions against your own domains:

```{r}
residue_regions_subset_summary(rr, regions = list(nterm = c(1, 100), cterm = c(101, 225)))
```
